models_evaluated: agentic LLM framework for rare disease diagnosis (reconstructed state-of-the-art)

links.outcome: Recall@1 of agentic LLM under strict cross-dataset isolation versus conventional one-vs-rest evaluation
links.effect: Cross-dataset mean Recall@1 fell from 54.3% (conventional one-vs-rest) to 40.3% with strict isolation (Hedges' g = 0.94); supervised classifiers dropped from 42.9% internal to 16.7% external (Cohen's d = 2.01).
links.quote: enforcing strict cross-dataset isolation resulted in a marked performance decline, with the cross-dataset mean Recall@1 decreasing from 54.3% (under conventional one-vs-rest evaluation) to 40.3% (Hedges' g = 0.94).

unlisted_practices: Strict cross-dataset isolation of candidate diagnosis space in rare disease AI evaluation
Screening clinical narratives for retrospective therapeutic cues that leak diagnoses
Aligning temporal versions of knowledge bases with evaluation cohorts

screen.reason: Empirical audit testing how data leakage and evaluation artifacts (e.g., candidate-space contamination, therapeutic cues) artificially inflate performance of LLMs in rare disease diagnosis, evaluating isolation protocols as evaluation safeguards.

primary.practice: data leakage auditing and cross-dataset isolation protocol
